title: Finite entity register for materials-disclosure drafting
purpose: Identity vocabulary and evidence-status distinctions. This is not a preparation disclosure, a claim of exhaustive physical possibilities, or evidence of patent coverage.
element_scope_notes: Recognized element names and symbols use the IUPAC table dated 4 May 2022, checked on the prepared date.
An accepted element identity does not establish stability, bulk availability, a known isotope for every A, or feasibility of every composition.
E119 through E138 are local placeholders, not accepted or systematic IUPAC symbols. The number 138 is a chosen indexing boundary, not a physical limit.
Isotopes, nuclear states, ions, allotropes and material phases are distinct identity layers and do not increase the recognized-element count.
No atomic weights, half-lives, synthesis conditions or material-property values are invented for hypothetical elements.

standard_model_particle_categories.counting_convention: Six quark flavor categories, three charged-lepton particle/antiparticle categories, three neutrino flavor categories, and five boson categories. W+ and W- are grouped; gluon color components are grouped. This is a table convention, not an absolute count of physical particles or quantum states.
standard_model_particle_categories.neutrino_note: Flavor labels differ from neutrino mass eigenstates. The register does not assert that the minimal massless-neutrino Standard Model explains observed neutrino masses, or resolve Dirac versus Majorana nature.
standard_model_particle_categories.limitations: Momentum, spin projections, polarization, color components, antiparticles, bound states, resonances, and hypothetical extensions are not an exhaustive cross-product. Established particle observation does not imply a stable bulk-material ingredient.

composite_particle_parameterization.scope: Examples include hadrons and nuclei; use a specific evaluated identity rather than treating all composites as one ingredient.
notes: A register that includes a nucleus and its nucleons must specify the construction level to avoid double-counting material constituents.
A resonance or short-lived particle is not automatically an isolable or persistent material.
Use PDG for hadrons and the isotope sources below for nuclei; this section does not enumerate every bound state.
These are host-dependent excitations; they are not additional chemical elements or freely interchangeable independent substances.
The example list is deliberately finite and does not enumerate all possible quasiparticles.

illustrative_families: other specified beyond-Standard-Model or dark-matter candidate models
notes: A search entry or numerical exclusion limit is not a discovery.
Do not assign measured masses, lifetimes, abundance or bulk-material behavior to an unconfirmed particle.
This parameterization does not claim to enumerate all theoretical particles, all models or all physically possible parameter values.

field_definitions.Z: Integer proton number. For a chemical-element nuclide, Z >= 1.
field_definitions.A: Integer nucleon count; A >= Z. This arithmetic condition is necessary, not evidence of existence.
field_definitions.state_local_id: Ground-state or source-qualified excited-state identifier, for example g or m1. This local label must be mapped to the source label and excitation information.
field_definitions.source_state_label: Preserve the exact original database designation; do not assume one source's m/n or m1/m2 conventions are globally identical.
field_definitions.excitation_energy: Value, unit, uncertainty and measured/estimated/unknown status where available; keep unresolved energy offsets.
field_definitions.existence_status: observed, unobserved_estimated, uncertain, reported_nonexistent, or not_assessed, following the actual evaluated source.
field_definitions.property_status: Assign measured, evaluated, estimated, limit, or unknown separately to each property.
field_definitions.electronic_charge_state: Optional separate qualifier; changing the electron population does not change Z, A or the nuclear-state identity.
field_definitions.source_provenance: Edition, record identifier, URL, evaluation cutoff, extraction date and original references where available.

rules: Unknown is not zero; preserve blank or unknown values.
Do not treat every algebraically permitted Z,A pair as an existing isotope.
An estimated mass does not by itself show that the nuclide is unobserved; existence and property status are separate.
Isomer states are not additional elements.
No complete nuclide table was fetched or enumerated for this artifact.
